scope: The standalone warm_compaction plugin, installed with the Hermes install command, on unpatched Hermes 45871e10, against the stock built-in compressor. Manual /compress and automatic compaction at the start of a turn. Ten synthetic cases at 100,000 or more prompt tokens per engine. One worker process per session, concurrency 1, no retry. DGX: protocol plugin-live-02. LM Studio: protocol plugin-live-03, which differs from plugin-live-02 only in the seed setup rule.
privacy: Metadata only: counts, codes, booleans, times, and hashes. No message text, request body, or key.

arms.plugin: context.engine warm_compaction: the installed and enabled plugin.
arms.stock: context.engine compressor: the built-in compressor and its auxiliary summary call on the same endpoint and model. The plugin is not installed.

modes.manual: Seed turn. Then /compress through the TUI path (tui_gateway _compress_session_history, then finalize_context_engine_compression_notification with committed=True, as the TUI does). Then the continuation turn.
modes.auto: Seed turn. Then the runner sets threshold_tokens to auto_threshold_tokens and threshold_percent to auto_threshold_tokens / context_length on the engine instance of the agent. The continuation turn then compacts in the Hermes turn-start preflight (agent/turn_context_compaction.py), before the new user message joins the history and before the first request of the turn.

protocol.order: One worker process per mode, case, and arm, sequential, concurrency 1. Manual mode for all cases first, then auto mode. In each mode the arm order alternates: plugin first for even case indexes, stock first for odd case indexes.
protocol.engine_order: LM Studio only. The DGX run of plugin-live-02 is complete and stays valid; this protocol does not repeat it. No other run on the engine during the run.

measures.time: Host wall time in the worker. Seed: the seed turn. Compaction: manual mode, _compress_session_history plus the finalize call; auto mode, the one _compress_context call inside the continuation turn. Continuation: manual mode, the continuation turn; auto mode, the continuation turn minus the compaction. Workflow = compaction + continuation.
measures.requests: Per HTTP request, metadata only: kind (main, warm, aux, fallback, other), times to headers and end, status, prompt, completion and cached tokens, finish reason, message count, and the SHA-256 of the messages. Hermes requests go through httpx. The plugin warm request goes through urllib and is recorded at that layer.
measures.prefix: A warm request keeps the prefix when the SHA-256 of its first k messages equals the SHA-256 of the messages of the seed request, where k is the message count of the seed request.
measures.warm_result: The warm_last record of the plugin engine: path, reason, elapsed_s, prompt_tokens, cached_tokens.
measures.next_action: cases.score_next_action of alpha-handoff-01 on the continuation reply.

stop_rules: A worker that exits non-zero, times out (1800 s), writes no result, or fails a step check stops the run.
Step checks: manual mode: /compress removes rows; auto mode: the continuation turn makes exactly one compaction; the continuation returns a reply.

Seed setup check: a normal seed turn adds the seed user row and one reply row, makes no compaction, keeps the session, and its last main request stops with a reply. A cut reply that Hermes retried to a normal end is normal. Any other seed turn is a setup failure, not a stop: the worker records the code (seed_reply_cut_at_token_limit, seed_turn_compacted, seed_turn_changed_history, seed_reply_missing, or seed_reply_incomplete) and the status setup_failed, skips the compaction and the continuation, and the run continues with the next session.
The seed request of the first session must report 90,000 to 125,000 prompt tokens, else the run stops.
A plugin-arm path other than warm (fallback or fixed summary) is a measured result, not a stop.

plugin-live-02: A worker that exits non-zero, times out (1800 s), writes no result, or fails a step check stops the run.

The seed request of the first session must report 90,000 to 125,000 prompt tokens, else the run stops.
A plugin-arm path other than warm (fallback or fixed summary) is a measured result, not a stop.

protocol_change.previous_run: plugin-live-02 (SHA-256 of its protocol.json fc268347e88c53153637651714cc0c86532086e3d3ccdbec393ee0fc6216a6be): the DGX run is complete (40 sessions). The LM Studio run stopped by its stop rule in session 17 (manual mode, case failed_check_choice_quoted_file_note, plugin arm) after 16 completed sessions. The seed reply of the 4B thinking model reached the 4096-token limit two times (the second time at 8192 tokens after the Hermes retry), so no seed request completed and the plugin had no capture. Hermes then compacted in the seed turn: the plugin used its fallback summary (reason no_capture), and the next request completed. The check 'the seed turn makes no compaction' stopped the run. The earlier alpha-hermes-live LM Studio run saw the same seed cut on this case. The 16 completed LM Studio sessions are a stopped run and are not used for decisions. This protocol changes one rule: a seed turn that does not end normally is a recorded setup failure, and the run continues. Everything else is the same as plugin-live-02.

host.key_config: For an engine with a key variable (DGX), model.key_env names that variable, as a user configures a custom endpoint key. Hermes auxiliary calls that do not get the agent runtime (the plugin fallback through ctx.llm) read the key from it. A no-network probe on the frozen Hermes copy showed the engine key with model.key_env and the placeholder key without it. The worker gives the variable and gives the key to AIAgent, as in plugin-live-01. The worker does not set OPENAI_API_KEY: Hermes does not read it for a configured custom endpoint.

decision_rules.works: Per engine and mode: the plugin arm takes the warm path (reason accepted) in at least 9 of 10 cases, and every accepted warm request keeps the prefix.
decision_rules.speed: Per engine and mode: the plugin workflow is faster than the stock workflow when its median is lower over the paired cases and it is lower in at least 7 of 10 paired cases. Report the compaction alone the same way.
decision_rules.cache: DGX: report the cached share of the warm request prompt. LM Studio: no cached-token counter, so report the cache as unknown and report the warm request time against the seed turn time of the same session.
decision_rules.quality: Report next-action passes per arm and mode. No content review is planned. The 4B model is not a quality reference.
decision_rules.setup_failures: A case with a setup failure in either arm is left out of the paired speed comparison. A plugin-arm setup failure counts as not accepted in the works rule: the count stays 9 of 10 cases. The report names each setup failure, and names a plugin-arm setup failure whose stock arm completed as a possible plugin effect.

stopped_runs.name: plugin-live-01
causes: Plugin defect: the capacity check estimated the whole warm request as UTF-8 bytes / 4 plus 10% (478,820 request bytes, about 131,700 estimated tokens). That is above the 131,072-token window, although the server measured 107,554 prompt tokens. The plugin refused the warm request.

Harness defect: the custom endpoint key was given only to AIAgent. Hermes auxiliary calls without the agent runtime (the plugin fallback through ctx.llm) then send the placeholder key no-key-required, and the DGX router answers 404 Not found. A user config names the key with model.key_env.
Plugin defect found during the analysis: the fallback transcript stopped at the first row that did not fit, so long rows left only the first user message and the two newest short rows.
stopped_runs.fixes: Commit db0efda (capacity from the reported prompt count; fallback transcript row cap). The next protocol (.work/plugin-live-02) adds model.key_env for the DGX engine.
stopped_runs.decision: The run stopped after the first session because the remaining 39 sessions would only measure the defects. This run gives no comparison result.

stopped_runs.name: plugin-live-02
stopped_runs.reason: The operator stopped the first LM Studio attempt between sessions. Its first two sessions took 188 s and 175 s, so 40 sessions would take about 121 minutes, which is longer than the 2-hour limit of the background task that ran it. The run started again as a detached process with a new output folder. The sessions of this attempt are not used.

stopped_runs.name: plugin-live-02
stopped_runs.cause: The seed reply of the 4B model reached the 4096-token limit (finish_reason length). Hermes sent the request again with 8192 output tokens, and that reply also reached the limit. No ordinary request of the session completed with stop, so the plugin had no capture. Hermes then started a compaction in the seed turn; the plugin used its fallback summary (reason no_capture), and the next request completed. The step check 'the seed turn makes no compaction' stopped the run. The earlier alpha-hermes-live LM Studio run saw the same seed cut on this case. This is a setup failure of the synthetic seed on a small thinking model, not a plugin defect.
stopped_runs.decision: The completed 16 sessions (8 manual case pairs) are reported as a stopped run and are not used for decisions. Protocol plugin-live-03 runs LM Studio again with one change: a seed-turn setup failure is recorded and the run continues. The DGX run of plugin-live-02 is complete and stays valid.

limits: One synthetic task family, one session shape (six large assistant rows), and the order effects of one server cache per engine.

In auto mode, the stock summary request can reuse the server cache of the manual stock summary request of the same case, and the DGX cache can hold requests of the earlier alpha runs. The recorded cached tokens show this. This bias favors the stock arm.
Results describe this plugin version on Hermes 45871e10 and these engine loads only. They do not prove M0, M3, deployed compatibility, or other models.

LM Studio ran 17 sessions of plugin-live-02 before this run. If its cache still holds an earlier request, the effect is as in plugin-live-02: it can make a stock summary request faster, which favors the stock arm. LM Studio reports no cached tokens, so this is unknown.
Automatic compaction ran at the start of a turn. The runs do not test the warm instruction after tool rows on a real chat template.
The plugin arm took the warm path in the accepted cases, so the runs do not measure the fallback summary quality.
The DGX run and the LM Studio run used two protocols. The only difference is the seed setup rule, and no DGX seed turn met a setup failure condition.
